content: The PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer is implemented with a deterministic surface sampler, joint and fixed-first search modes, and a shared coarse-to-fine engine, but the reviewer rates it as not yet production-ready for complex imported sets (algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10). Key blockers: (1) imported SceneObject clearance uses the entire object AABB, so origins inside the AABB get zero clearance and are rejected, which can eliminate all legal candidates for large imported rooms; the fix is actual geometry clearance via the coverage BVH. (2) Geometry representation uses JavaScript objects/arrays and 64-bit numbers, is structured-cloned into the worker, and allocates many temporary arrays during raycasts, causing GC pressure and likely freezing/crashes on heavy imports; the fix is compact typed arrays and transferable ArrayBuffers, plus a better BVH. (3) extractCoverageScene runs synchronously on the main thread before the worker is used, so scene recreation, flattening, transforms, disposal, and cloning can freeze the UI before any progress event. (4) The UI can rewrite origins on existing panorama references, but changing metadata does not transform the already-captured image, ruining alignment; the correct workflow is to capture/render new panoramas at the optimized origins and import them. (5) reachableCoverage and final combined coverage are computed on different sample banks (coarse vs fine with seed+1), so the UI can show impossible ratios; for fixed-first the fixed origin is also excluded from the reachable upper bound. (6) Fixed-first mode does not enforce minimumOriginSeparation, so a near-duplicate second origin can be returned. Additional issues: the four-level refinement is a multiresolution neighborhood sample around the original seed rather than a true iterative refinement that recenters after each level; local offsets can float between floors because Y is preserved without re-projecting onto the floor under the new X/Z; the optimizer evaluates angle/texel quality but the runtime shader blends only by distance, so optimized and visible results can diverge. The reviewer recommends preserving the high-level design and applying seven fixes: replace AABB clearance with geometry clearance, use typed arrays/transferable buffers, move extraction into the worker, remove the ability to relocate existing panorama references, compute reported metrics on one common sample bank, enforce separation in fixed-first mode, and reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. A follow-up instruction set a goal to rebase onto main, add an allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor filtering, run a real complex imported-set benchmark plus a full 100k+ optimizer integration test, and repeatedly spawn a subagent to disprove completeness until no holes remain. Subsequent work removed a stale distance-only blend test, replaced it with assertions guarding the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes, and the targeted regression passed; a full unit/lint/build run then passed with 42 test files and 371 tests, including a 100k+ triangle projection coverage engine test and real WebGL pixel-readback gates for occlusion cubemaps, projected-style compile, receiving projected materials, and projected receive behavior.

Git status shows 16 files changed (307 insertions, 216 deletions), origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD, and new untracked files docs/coverage-optimizer-benchmark.md and scripts/coverage-import-benchmark.mjs are present. The surface sampler now includes imported-floor filtering with constants MIN_IMPORTED_FLOOR_AREA_SQUARE_METERS=2.5, MIN_IMPORTED_FLOOR_LONG_SPAN_METERS=1.5, MIN_IMPORTED_FLOOR_SHORT_SPAN_METERS=0.65, a union-find based filterImportedFloorComponents function that groups connected upward triangles and keeps only components meeting area and span thresholds, with the largest component as a deterministic fallback if no components pass. extractCoverageScene is now async, chunked between objects and large buffer ranges with yieldToMainThread calls, copying position attributes in chunks of 262,144 values to avoid monopolizing the browser event loop before worker optimization begins.

The PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer was rebased onto main and hardened for complex imported sets. Key fixes include replacing AABB-based clearance with geometry clearance via the coverage BVH, moving extractCoverageScene to an async chunked worker flow with yieldToMainThread and 262,144-value position copy chunks, adding imported-floor filtering via union-find with MIN_IMPORTED_FLOOR_AREA_SQUARE_METERS=2.5, MIN_IMPORTED_FLOOR_LONG_SPAN_METERS=1.5, MIN_IMPORTED_FLOOR_SHORT_SPAN_METERS=0.65, using one common fine validation bank for reachable and combined coverage metrics, enforcing minimumOriginSeparation in fixed-first mode, and reprojecting local refinement candidates onto their floor. The reviewer's seven recommended fixes were applied while preserving the high-level design. A real imported-set benchmark used a 171,156,440-byte Blender 4.5 splash GLB (191 mesh nodes, 36,788 triangles) with 164 candidates and 24,576 fine validation samples, yielding 0.47s import, 36.90s optimizer time, 63.2% combined coverage, 69.4% reachable upper bound, 91.0% reachable efficiency, and no browser errors on an AMD Ryzen 7 3700X with Chrome 150.0.7871.127. Automated gates are green: 371 unit/integration tests across 42 test files including both optimizer modes over 101,250 triangles, TypeScript, production build, and real WebGL compile/pixel checks for occlusion cubemaps, projected-style compile, receiving projected materials, and projected receive behavior. The first audit disproved completion on those two points; the response was to fix the substantive issue with an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism (so ambiguous large horizontal surfaces are user-constrained instead of guessed) plus the auditor's large-top regression, and to publish only after that revision passes and a fresh auditor cannot find a hole.

The build completed successfully (1777 modules transformed). The patch added a disabled prop to the Toggle component and disabled the floor region toggle and all six number fields when status === 'running'. The E2E scenario was updated to fill valid Y bounds after the invalid case, assert the analyze button is enabled, click analyze, assert the toggle and all six floor min/max fields are disabled during the run, wait for the result, then assert the toggle is enabled again.
